latest_release.name: v0.24.3
latest_release.body:
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jnunemaker/httparty/compare/v0.24.2...v0.24.3

## Bug Fixes

- Support the `json` gem 3.x, which removed the `quirks_mode` parser option. (#846)
- Fix the `MultiXml` deprecation warning with multi_xml 0.9+. (#838, thanks @robzolkos)
- A UTF-8 byte order mark (BOM) is now stripped from responses that don't declare a charset. Before, a BOM-prefixed JSON response without a charset raised `JSON::ParserError`. (#852)
- A response body that is only a BOM, or a BOM followed by whitespace, now parses to `nil` like any other blank body, instead of raising or returning the whitespace. (#851, thanks @januththedev)
- `parsed_response` and `response.body` are separate strings for UTF-8 text responses, as in 0.24.2. (#854)

## Performance

- `raise_on` with a Range (e.g. `500..599`) checks the range directly instead of building a regex for every code in it. (#843, thanks @MaxLap)
- Parsing allocates fewer objects per response. (#854)

## Behavior Changes

For `text/plain`, `text/html` and `text/csv` responses **without a charset**, a leading BOM is now removed from `parsed_response`, matching what already happened when `charset=utf-8` was set. If you worked around the BOM by matching it (for example a CSV header of `"\xEF\xBB\xBFid"`), that match will now be `"id"`. Workarounds like `delete_prefix("﻿")` keep working.

These are unchanged: `response.body` and `to_s` (raw bytes), `application/octet-stream` and other formats HTTParty doesn't parse, and bodies declared in other charsets such as ISO-8859-1 or UTF-16.

## Other

- Specs no longer need a UTF-8 locale. (#853)
- README and example updates. (#836, thanks @harland-davis; #837, thanks @zed-0xff)
